bodyweightSquat.purpose: Practice the squat without an external load and link comfortable range with a full standing finish.
setup: Place feet around shoulder width, generally forward.
Reach the arms forward around shoulder height to help keep the chest lifted.
steps: Inhale as the arms lift; lower through a controlled comfortable range.
Keep heels grounded, knees tracking outward and chest lifted.
Stand all the way up and finish the hips; lower the arms between reps if needed.
bracing: The demonstration cues an inhale with arms up. No universal breath count is specified.
mistakes: Rocking forward or lifting the heels: reduce range and regain a stable base.
Stopping short at the top: return to full comfortable standing before another rep.

evidence.quote: the important part of this is that you finish your hips at the top

stepBackLunge.purpose: Practice a controlled step-back lunge while the lead foot stays stable.
setup: Start around shoulder width with feet generally forward.
Keep elbows near the body, as though holding a tool in front.
steps: Step one foot back without a preliminary foot shuffle.
Use a comfortable controlled depth, keeping the lead heel grounded and trunk aligned.
Return to full standing, finishing the hips and knee; alternate and match the legs.
bracing: Maintain controlled crown-to-tailbone alignment. The source does not specify exact breath timing.
mistakes: Lead heel lifting: shorten or adjust the step and work in a controllable range.
Leaning or failing to finish standing: reduce demand and restore alignment before another rep.

evidence.quote: in the progression of lunges we start with a step back lunge

doubleClean.purpose: Practice the hard-style double kettlebell clean and safe return to the ground.
setup: Use a familiar matched pair with enough stance clearance for both bells.
Place bells in front and use the corner grip; do not use a bent barbell-style wrist.
steps: Hike back with thumbs back and drive through the hips to a stable standing rack.
Keep the catch controlled, wrists aligned and hands from colliding.
Brace in the rack, then reverse the hike to park both bells under control in their starting position.
bracing: The source cues engaged abs, squeezed glutes and breathing behind the shield in the hard-style catch.
mistakes: Knuckles colliding: use a lighter familiar pair and rebuild synchronized control.
Dropping the bells: finish and park them under control instead.
Soft-style versus hard-style catch: this page describes only the demonstrated hard-style option.
doubleClean.coverage: partial: hard-style transcript outline; paired clearance and catch still require visual verification

complexCleanPress.purpose: Combine a familiar single-arm clean and strict press while preserving the rack between components.
setup: Use a familiar light bell and an established clean/press technique.
Pick up with two hands to inspect the rack: forearm vertical, elbow near hip, thumb near collarbone.
steps: Use the hips to clean the bell into a controlled rack.
Press to controlled lockout without losing trunk position.
Lower fully to the rack before the next clean; park with control and match sides.
bracing: The demonstration cues ribs down and glute engagement in the press.
mistakes: Cleaning with the elbow away from the body: rebuild the close, quiet rack.
Starting the next clean before lowering fully: return the elbow near the hip and thumb near collarbone first.

evidence.quote: elbow always comes back to hip

complexCleanPress.coverage: partial: combined technique outline; dose/rest are app defaults and visual review remains necessary

complexCleanSquatPress.purpose: An app-programmed single-arm clean, rack squat and press combination using familiar components.
setup: Use a load controlled in every component and review the single-rack squat separately.
steps: Clean into a secure rack.
Perform the familiar single-rack squat and stand fully.
Press from that rack, lower under control, then repeat and match sides.
bracing: Keep controlled bracing through transitions. No exact breath sequence is established by these combined sources.
mistakes: Treating goblet-squat experience as proof of single-rack control: review the distinct rack position before combining.
Rushing a weak component: practice it separately; do not raise load through the complex.

evidence.quote: The single kettlebell version of this

complexCleanSquatPress.coverage: partial: app combination of reviewed components; #335 gives only brief single-bell context

complexDoubleCleanSquatPress.purpose: Combine a controlled double clean, double front squat and press from the same rack.
setup: Use a familiar matched pair; the component skills and double rack must already be established.
Start bells in front, leave handle clearance and hinge to a controlled hike.
steps: Clean to the double rack.
Squat with controlled rack and knee clearance, then stand fully.
Press from that rack without another intervening clean; lower both bells under control.
Return through the hinge to park in the starting position.
bracing: The source cues glute engagement at the overhead finish and a stable rack between cycles.
mistakes: Uncontrolled elbow/knee contact or collapsed rack: practice the separate squat first.
Mixing clean–press–squat with clean–squat–press: keep the chosen sequence consistent in the log.
Dropping the bells: park them with a controlled return.

evidence.quote: It is a clean. It is a squat. It is a press.

complexDoubleCleanSquatPress.coverage: partial: full sequence described in transcript; clearance and transitions need visual confirmation

bearCrawl.purpose: Travel on hands and feet with opposite-limb coordination; an instructional reference rather than an automatic endurance prescription.
setup: Begin in a comfortable kneeling/child-position setup.
Tuck toes and move toward a comfortable down-dog-like position; do not force hamstring range.
steps: Move an opposite hand and foot forward with controlled support.
Travel only as far as the surface and technique safely allow.
Stop or return to stationary practice when support or coordination changes.
bracing: The source describes cross-body stabilization. Exact breathing timing is not specified.
mistakes: Forcing straight knees or short hand/foot distance: keep a comfortable individual range.
Using an unsafe surface: choose clear stable ground and protect hands as appropriate.
bearCrawl.name: Bear crawl
qualifications: The source presents bear crawl before cat crawl. This is a teaching relationship, not automatic skill certification.
Four minutes under tension followed by one minute rest is a source example, not a beginner default or a workout assigned here.

catCrawl.purpose: Low-knee quadruped travel, taught as a more demanding extension of bear-crawl coordination.
setup: Start on hands and knees with toes tucked.
Hover knees around one to two inches from the ground only while comfortable and controlled.
steps: Keep the spine approximately parallel to the floor and knees around a right angle.
Move opposite hand and leg, maintaining the low knee hover.
Use a short controlled practice period; return to grounded support when position fails.
bracing: Maintain stable trunk support; the transcript does not establish a universal breath pattern.
mistakes: Knees rising high or trunk losing position: return to stationary/earlier practice.
Treating advanced rails, stairs or height examples as entry practice: remain on safe ground.

evidence.quote: Whatever time under tension you do to start this movement

catCrawl.name: Cat crawl
qualifications: The source discusses a four-minute goal, one-minute work/rest examples, and 60% of an observed controlled duration. These are contexts, not one universal dose.
No baseline test or automatic 60% calculation is added by this reference. Bear-crawl teaching is earlier context; eligibility is not automatically granted.

doubleClubInside.purpose: Alternate inside circles while controlling a separate club in each hand.
setup: Use familiar light clubs in clear space and an established order position.
Keep forearms vertical and a strong wrist; establish control before moving either club.
steps: Make the inside circle on one side while limiting unintended movement of the other club.
Return to a controlled stop and regain balance before alternating.
Match the sides and stop when the resting club can no longer be stabilized.
bracing: The source describes radiating trunk tension and glute involvement as one club stops and the other accelerates.
mistakes: Letting the held club wobble or escape: lower demand and rebuild control.
Treating two clubs as equivalent to two hands on one club: these are different coordination demands.

evidence.quote: double Club is always the hardest

doubleClubInside.coverage: partial: source-reviewed outline; paired-club equipment/programming and visual technique validation remain incomplete
doubleClubInside.name: Double-club alternating inside circles
qualifications: The source places double-club work after single/two-hand experience and calls it more complex. It does not establish a universal two-year waiting rule.
This reference does not schedule paired-club sets or claim compatibility with kettlebell-pair equipment settings.

doubleClubOutside.purpose: Alternate outside circles with two clubs while maintaining a controlled double order position.
setup: Review familiar double inside-circle control first.
Establish vertical forearms, controlled wrists and feet generally forward; do not collapse the rack or flare the ribs.
steps: Rotate and perform one outside circle while stabilizing the held club.
Return to a stable catch before the other side.
Keep transitions controlled; reduce demand when the held club wobbles.
bracing: The source cues ribs down, glute engagement and stable lower-trunk tension.
mistakes: Overtracking or letting the held club tip: rebuild the movement with lighter familiar tools.
Confusing numerical bodybuilding examples with a beginner prescription: no sets are assigned by this reference.

evidence.quote: the double outside circle is harder than the double inside circle
